## Abstract
This report presents a search for expression studies related to heat-shock response in Escherichia coli from the NCBI GEO database. Using a keyword and organism-filtered search restricted to expression profiling series (GSE), 50 studies were identified, of which 20 results were initially retrieved with detailed metadata for 10 studies due to response size limits. Study metadata includes accession numbers, titles, experiment types, sample counts, and supplementary file access links. These studies cover a range of heat-shock related gene expression profiling experiments in E. coli, including RNA-seq and microarray data, and provide valuable resources for investigating bacterial stress responses at the transcriptomic level.

## I. Introduction
Background: Heat shock response in Escherichia coli is a critical biological pathway allowing survival and adaptation to elevated temperatures, affecting gene expression regulation. Analyzing transcriptomic data from heat-shock studies informs understanding of stress physiology and proteostasis in this model bacterium.

Literature Review: The retrieved GEO entries illustrate a spectrum of studies investigating heat-shock microproteins, regulatory networks, chaperone machinery, transcriptional responses to temperature shifts, and genomic architecture changes under heat stress.

Knowledge Gap: Before this query, a comprehensive compilation of expression profiling studies specifically targeting heat shock in E. coli was not readily available in a single list to facilitate systematic analysis or meta-studies.

Objective & Hypothesis: To compile a comprehensive list of gene expression studies focusing on heat-shock response in E. coli, expected to reveal a broad dataset collection covering various experimental designs and conditions relevant to bacterial heat shock.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design: Search of NCBI GEO repository metadata for E. coli expression studies related to heat shock, filtered by organism and keyword "heat-shock," limited to GEO Series (GSE) records.

Materials: NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) database queried via the geo_search tool.

Procedures: The search parameters were organism set to "Escherichia coli," term set to "heat-shock," entry_type set to "gse" for expression profiling series, with maximum results capped at 20 for initial retrieval.

Statistical Analysis: Total matching studies counted as 50; metadata extracted for 10 detailed records due to API context size limits, including accession, sample count, and experiment type.

## III. Results

| GSE269907 | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock               | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing| 12           | 2026/02/09       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE269nnn/GSE269907/        |
| GSE305556 | Mechanisms of assembly and function of the Hsp70-Hsp40 chaperone machinery                                 | Other                                           | 12           | 2025/10/15       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305556/        |
| GSE305476 | Deciphering Host Stress Responses for Predictable Heterologous Gene Expression in E. coli                  | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing| 74           | 2025/08/21       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305476/        |
| GSE283264 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RNA-Seq)                                 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing| 25           | 2025/06/24       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/        |

| GSE272160 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RedC)                                   | Other                                           | 4            | 2025/06/24       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/        |
| GSE272159 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (MicroC)                                 | Other                                           | 33           | 2025/06/24       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/        |
| GSE272158 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (HiC)                                    | Other                                           | 2            | 2025/06/24       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/        |
| GSE289056 | Thermally adapted Escherichia coli keeps transcriptomic response during temperature upshift exposure      | Expression profiling by array                    | 4            | 2025/05/29       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE289nnn/GSE289056/        |

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation: The search successfully identified a substantial number of heat-shock related expression series in E. coli, covering diverse experimental angles from microproteins, chaperones, genomic organization, to thermal adaptation. 

Context: These retrieved studies with detailed metadata enable researchers to locate raw and processed data files via FTP links for deeper analysis and comparative studies.

Limitations: The initial output truncation (10 out of 50 studies detailed) means the full list is larger; for complete data, further queries or refined searches are needed. The detailed expression values are only accessible from supplementary files in the GEO FTP repository, not directly via the API.

Conclusion & Future Directions: This dataset compilation forms a foundation for meta-analyses and hypothesis generation on E. coli heat-shock biology. Next steps could include full retrieval of all 50 studies, extraction of expression matrices, and investigation of differential expression patterns across conditions.
